newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Philippine tuna opens new market for Fedex.
newsitem.headline: Philippine tuna opens new market for Fedex.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said it has opened up a new market in the Philippines flying fresh tuna to Japan via its Subic Bay hub.

"This is opening up a whole new market for us and we are doing very well. It's a great product for us because of it's weight, tuna means very good revenue," FedEx Vice President South Pacific region John Allison told Reuters.
He declined to give detailed tonnage figures.

"The market has evolved for us in the past year and it has been created because of our Subic Bay hub which opened last year. We have used a third party airline bringing the fish in from the southern Philippines or Indonesia and into Subic and it's then quickly freighted onto Japan," he added.
Fedex say their overnight service from the Philippines offers first arrival at Japanese markets at around 0300 local time in Osaka and slightly later at Tokyo's Narita airport.
The U.S. firm says it is expecting to face increasing competition from new airlines in the Philippines which are keen to eventually open up new direct routes to Japan.

Fish exporters are also able to use new airport facilities in the southern Philippines such as General Santos airport in Mindanao and a new airport which is nearing completion in the fish rich island of Cebu from where new, direct flights are expected.

But frustrated carriers such as cargo airline Pacific East Asia Cargo (PEAC) say Japan has stalled negotiations on new routes for the past three years. --Air Cargo News Room Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+44-171-542-5017
